details: Bitcoin experienced a sharp surge and subsequent crash over the weekend due to conflicting announcements regarding the Strait of Hormuz. Initially, reports of Iran's foreign minister announcing the strait's reopening led Bitcoin to rally past $78,000. However, less than 24 hours later, Iran's state-run Nour News Agency declared the waterway returned to "strict management and control," causing Bitcoin to plummet back below $76,000. This rapid reversal highlights cryptocurrency's sensitivity to geopolitical shocks, resulting in over $762 million in total liquidations.
sourceName: CoinGlass (as cited by the search snippet which references Nour News Agency and Bloomberg)
title: Bitcoin Plunges as Iran Reverses Strait of Hormuz Reopening

details: Iran has reportedly demanded that ships pay tolls in cryptocurrency for accessing the Strait of Hormuz. This development comes as the waterway has become a flashpoint in the ongoing U.S. conflict with the Middle Eastern nation, with the U.S. military instituting a blockade of Iranian ports this week. The demand for crypto tolls underscores the increasing role of digital assets in geopolitical conflicts and potential sanctions evasion.
title: Iran Demands Crypto Tolls for Strait Passage
